t: What Cable Management Sleeves and Braided Tubing Are
title: What Cable Management Sleeves and Braided Tubing Are
description: Cable sleeves gather a multi-wire bundle into one clean tube — braided PET sleeving that expands over connectors, or neoprene zippered sleeves that wrap around existing runs. Instead of five visible cables, you see one tidy trunk. For PC builders they turn the visible runs (behind the case window, under the desk) from spaghetti into a single intentional line.

demo.program:
print("Sleeve = many cables in, one clean trunk out.")
print("Braided PET: expands over connectors, cut to length.")
print("Neoprene zippered: wraps existing runs (no disconnecting).")
print("Visible runs -> one intentional line, not spaghetti.")

t: Braided PET Sleeving: The Expandable Standard
title: Braided PET Sleeving: The Expandable Standard
description: Braided PET (polyethylene terephthalate) sleeving is the standard: it expands to about 150% of its resting diameter to slip over connectors, then contracts to hug the bundle. Sold by resting diameter (1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1 inch) on spools; brands like Alex Tech are popular. Cut with a hot knife or sear the ends with a lighter — raw cuts fray into a mess within days.

demo.program:
print("PET braid: expands ~150% over connectors, contracts to hug bundle.")
print("Sizes by resting diameter: 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1 in (Alex Tech popular).")
print("Cut HOT (hot knife / seared ends): raw cuts fray in days.")

title: Neoprene Zippered Sleeves: No-Disconnect Wrapping
description: Neoprene sleeves with a zipper wrap around cables already connected — no unplugging everything to thread a braid. JOTO-style sleeves are the common pick for under-desk runs: lay the cables in, zip closed, done. They look clean and install in minutes, but add bulk and trap heat — fine for desk cables, less ideal inside hot cases.

demo.program:
print("Zippered neoprene: wraps CONNECTED runs (no unplugging).")
print("JOTO-style: under-desk favorite, minutes to install.")
print("Bulkier + traps heat: desk = great, hot case interior = think twice.")

t: Sizing Sleeves to Bundles: The Diameter Math
title: Sizing Sleeves to Bundles: The Diameter Math
description: Size the sleeve's resting diameter to about 80% of the bundle's diameter — the braid expands over connectors during install, then grips. Too big and it slides and bunches; too small and it will not pass the connectors. Measure the bundle with calipers or a string, add connector clearance, pick the size. One size per trunk beats one giant sleeve for everything.

demo.program:
bundles = [(0.4, "fan wires"), (0.8, "SATA group"), (1.2, "PSU trunk")]
for dia, name in bundles:
    print(f"  {name:<10} bundle {dia} in -> sleeve ~{dia*0.8:.2f} in resting")
print("Rule: resting diameter ~= 80% of bundle. Measure, don't guess.")

t: Installing Braided Sleeve: Thread, Expand, Finish
title: Installing Braided Sleeve: Thread, Expand, Finish
description: The install: disconnect one end, bunch the cables, expand the braid over the connectors (a pull-through string helps on long runs), slide it down, and finish both ends — heat-shrink tubing over the sleeve ends gives the pro look and stops fraying. For runs you cannot disconnect, slit the braid lengthwise and wrap it (or use zippered neoprene instead).

demo.program:
print("1. disconnect one end, bunch cables")
print("2. expand braid over connectors (pull-string for long runs)")
print("3. slide down, finish ends with HEAT-SHRINK (pro look, no fray)")
print("Can't disconnect? slit braid lengthwise OR use zippered neoprene.")

title: Heat-Shrink Finishing: The Pro Edge
description: Heat-shrink tubing over sleeve ends is what separates clean from DIY-looking: slide 2:1 shrink over the braid end, heat gently with a heat gun (hair dryer works), and it clamps the braid permanently. Add a printed label under clear shrink for labeled trunks. Keep the heat moving — parked heat melts the braid. The finish takes minutes and lasts the build's life.

demo.program:
print("2:1 shrink over braid ends + gentle heat = clamped, pro finish.")
print("Clear shrink + printed label underneath = labeled trunks.")
print("Keep heat MOVING: parked heat melts braid. Minutes to do, lasts years.")

title: Use Case: Under-Desk Trunks
description: Under the desk, a zippered neoprene sleeve turns the monitor-power-USB tangle into one trunk from desk to floor — the single most visible cable improvement in a setup. Size it to the bundle, zip it, anchor both ends with clips. Adding a cable later means unzipping, laying in, re-zipping: the maintenance that keeps desks clean long-term.

t: Use Case: Test Bench and Lab Cable Runs
title: Use Case: Test Bench and Lab Cable Runs
description: Test benches breed cable nests; sleeving the semi-permanent runs (PSU trunk, monitor, network) keeps the bench usable while test leads stay free. Use split-loom or zippered sleeves here — bench configurations change too often for permanent braid. The rule: sleeve the infrastructure, leave the experiments loose.

t: Sleeve Materials Compared: PET, Nylon, Neoprene, Split-Loom
title: Sleeve Materials Compared: PET, Nylon, Neoprene, Split-Loom
description: PET braid: the standard — expandable, clean, needs disconnecting. Nylon multifilament: softer, premium feel, pricier. Neoprene zippered: no-disconnect, bulky, warm. Split-loom corrugated: cheapest, rugged, industrial look — great for behind-desk and garage, ugly in a windowed case. Match material to visibility and change frequency.

print("nylon multi : softer, premium, pricier")

print("split-loom  : cheap, rugged, industrial (behind desk, not in window)")

t: Heat and Airflow: Sleeving Inside Cases
title: Heat and Airflow: Sleeving Inside Cases
description: Sleeving inside a case slightly reduces airflow around the bundled cables — negligible for data cables, worth thinking about for a fat PSU trunk in a hot case. Do not sleeve individual high-heat runs (like GPU power in a mining-hot case) in insulating neoprene; PET braid breathes better. Sleeve for looks where air is plentiful, and keep hot zones breathing.

demo.program:
print("Sleeving trims airflow around bundle: negligible for data, note for PSU trunks.")
print("Hot cases: PET breathes, neoprene insulates. Don't neoprene hot runs.")
print("Looks where air is plentiful; breathing room where it's hot.")

title: Maintenance: Cleaning and Re-Sleeving
description: Braided sleeves collect dust — vacuum with a brush attachment or blast with the duster; neoprene wipes clean with a damp cloth. When re-cabling, slit old braid off (it is consumable) and re-sleeve fresh — trying to reuse expanded braid gives a baggy fit. Keep a spool of the common size on hand; re-sleeving a trunk takes twenty minutes.

print("Re-cable: slit old braid off (consumable), re-sleeve fresh.")
print("Reused expanded braid = baggy fit. Keep a spool of the common size.")

t: Buying Guide: Spools, Kits, and Colors
title: Buying Guide: Spools, Kits, and Colors
description: Buy PET by the spool (25-50 ft) in your two most-used sizes — 1/2 and 3/4 inch cover most PC work — plus a heat-shrink assortment. Kits with multiple colors tempt, but black plus one theme color beats a rainbow drawer. Expect 10-20 dollars per spool; the heat-shrink kit is another 10. One spool handles many builds.

demo.program:
print("Spools: 25-50 ft, 1/2 + 3/4 in (cover most PC work). $10-20/spool.")
print("Plus: heat-shrink assortment (~$10). Black + 1 theme color > rainbow drawer.")
print("One spool = many builds. Buy sizes, not kits.")

title: Advanced: Custom-Sleeved PSU Cables
description: The show-build pinnacle is fully custom-sleeved PSU cables — each wire individually sleeved in paracord or PET, combed straight, custom lengths. It takes hours and a pin-removal tool, but the result is the cleanest cabling possible. Warning: pinouts vary by PSU — sleeving the wrong pinout or mixing cables between PSU brands can kill hardware. Custom cables are expert territory with real risk.

print("Never mix modular cables between PSU brands. Expert territory, real risk.")

title: The Complete Sleeving Discipline

Many cables in, one intentional trunk out — every visible run, every time.
